Food seasoning: salt.

Food ingredients for the dog:
One piece of connective tissue and two meat scraps.
Mixing it with them.

Separately, connective tissue for the dog.
</post>

<explanation>
The first heading establishes food-seasoning purpose. The ingredients heading makes the counted tissue and scraps food ingredients for the dog; "it" and "them" resolve to that piece and those two scraps. Salt and connective tissue can have nonfood uses. Tissue "for the dog" specifies a recipient, not a food role; it could be for a training scent. Those unrestricted headings stay outside Food and Dog food. The two ingredient subjects, their expressed group and complete mixing action retain their counts and roles beneath every compatible parent copy, including both Dog food branches. Separate Salt, Connective tissue, Meat scraps and Dogs subjects remain alongside the action. The separate recipient clause adds no ingredient relationship.
</explanation>

<post>
Chair repair:
One steel plate and two steel bolts.
Attaching it with them to the chair.
</post>

<explanation>
The heading supplies chair-repair purpose. "it" refers to the one steel plate; "them" refers to the two steel bolts. Steel plates, steel bolts and chairs remain subjects alongside the attachment. A plate, bolts or their attachment could instead be for another purpose, so the unrestricted material and attachment headings stay outside Chair repair. The complete repair-material group belongs beneath every copy of both qualified counted materials. The complete attachment states the same counted materials and repair purpose; it belongs beneath every group copy and every compatible material, chair and action heading. Placement in another branch cannot fill a missing copy.
</explanation>
